Menara Taming Sari (Melaka Tower) is located at Bandar Hilir (Sari City), not far from Melaka in Kuala Selangor (Malacca).
It was opened in 1866 to commemorate the five-week-long revolt in Malacca against the Dutch. A prominent colonial traffic hub during the mid-nineteenth century, Melaka Tower was even employed in a still-famous escapade my Operation Penton by the Malay rulers: they relocated to their capitals here in the early twentieth century from (for the Malay leaders) Pulau Hormos (Nusa Penida), about 200 km (124 miles) to the west.
Like Malacca (Portugal), Melaka (Malaccan: merlús dás, 'plains' or 'tains') was discovered by the Arabs in the thirteenth century, which is not surprising since Malcolm of Algonquian descent shared a common origin with our Islamic ancestors, also with the Basques, to which Melaka is considered the former "tiersprop" between Southeast Asia and Europe.
